hypotheses.justification: The proof only uses `hs` so that it can rewrite with `restrict_apply_eq_zero'`. That rewrite turns `ν.restrict A B = 0` into `ν (B ∩ A) = 0`, where `A = {y | (x,y) ∈ s}`. Only the inequality is needed, and Mathlib's `Measure.le_restrict_apply (s t : Set α) : μ (t ∩ s) ≤ μ.restrict s t` gives it with no measurability assumption. Proof without `hs`: use `hbad.exists_measurable_subset_ae_eq` to get a measurable `t ⊆ s \ G` with `t =ᵐ s \ G`. By `Measure.measure_prod_null htmeas` (which needs `SFinite ν`, still available), it is enough to show `ν (Prod.mk x ⁻¹' t) = 0` for every x. We have `Prod.mk x ⁻¹' t ⊆ Prod.mk x ⁻¹' (s \ G) = {y | (x,y) ∉ G} ∩ {y | (x,y) ∈ s}`. By `le_restrict_apply`, the measure of that set is at most `ν.restrict {y | (x,y) ∈ s} {y | (x,y) ∉ G}`, which is 0 by `ae_iff` applied to `hsection x`. Then `measure_congr htae.symm` finishes as in the current proof. Measurability of `s` is not needed anywhere else, and no degenerate case depends on it.

`Measure.prod` is defined as `if SFinite ν then bind μ (fun x => map (Prod.mk x) ν) else 0` (`protected irreducible_def prod` in Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Measure/Prod.lean). The statement still elaborates without the instance, since `Measure.prod` and `NullMeasurableSet _ (μ.prod ν)` take no instance argument. Proof without it: split on `SFinite ν` by cases. If it holds, apply the existing proof with that instance. If not, `rw [Measure.prod_def, if_neg h]` makes `μ.prod ν = 0`, so `μ.prod ν (s \ G) = 0` holds trivially. This hypothesis can be removed independently of `hs`.
